To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the shrimp waste is rich source of carotenoid and protein and the enzyme-assisted extraction process can be successfully applied to extract the carotenoids from the shrimp head waste.

the shrimp head waste is a good source of carotenoid and its extraction can be done using different proteolytics enzymes and the extracted carotenoid can be used as source of carotenod and antioxidant.

the carotenoid-proteins complex from shrimp head wastes can be extracted by using proteolytic enzymes and the carotenoids can be recovered from the carotenoid proteins complex by using organic solvents and/or supercritical CO 2.
In summary, our research is concerned with
a new approach for the utilization of shrimp waste as a source of protein and carotenoids, which could be used as a functional ingredient in various food products.

the development of an enzymatic extraction process for the recovery of carotenoids in the shrimp head waste and also the development of a novel carotenoid-proteins complex (CPC) from shrimp head waste.
the development of an environmentally friendly and efficient process for the extraction of carotenoid from shrimp wastes.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the enzymatic extraction process of carotenoid from shrimp waste was found to be more efficient and eco-friendly than the conventional methods.
the use of enzymes for the isolation of carotenoids-protein complex from different head wastes of shrimps is an attractive option.
the enzymatic isolation of CPC from shrimp waste and its use for the extraction of carotenoid is an efficient and promising technology.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the carotenoids from frozen CPC and freeze dried CPC can be used as a natural food colorant and also as a natural antioxidant.

the enzymatic isolation of carotinoid-protein complex is a promising alternative to the traditional solvent and SC–CO2 extractions and the carotenoids recovered from CPC are stable enough for use as natural antioxidants.

shrimp head waste can be a good source of carotenoid, and the enzyme-assisted extraction method is an alternative for the extraction of carotenoid and the freeze-dried CPC can be an alternative source for natural antioxidants.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the shrimp head waste can be a good source of carotenoid and protein, and can be used as natural food colorants.
the carotenoid-rich CPC can be used as natural source of antioxidant in various applications such as food, feed, pharmaceuticals and cosmetic industries.
the carotenoids extracted using proteolytic enzymes are more stable than those extracted by traditional solvent and SC–CO2 extraction methods.
